notes.scope: Eight components — exactly the 7 backend services + Next.js frontend named in BA spec. No additions, no omissions. Refactored from dry-run #1 to (a) add identity.profile.read to checkout's dependency list (REV-L2-001 buyerEmail dataflow), (b) add the formally authored order.create-from-checkout + order.cancel-on-checkout-failure contracts to checkout + order's dependency lists (REV-L2-001/004 closure), and (c) keep every complexity != standard tagged with complexity_rationale (validator enforces).

complexity_rationale_legend.complex: inventory (concurrent reservation, no-negative invariant under load, dual sync+async paths, in-process expiry sweeper + outbox), checkout (multi-service orchestration with 8-step + compensation + idempotency + server-side pricing tier + buyerEmail dataflow), order (state machine + transitions + outbox + cross-service consumers + sole-writer rule + state-driven event handling for the PR-003 cross-topic race), payment (idempotent webhook with strict (paymentIntentId, providerStatus) dedup AND outbox event emission), frontend-web (PR-007: 34 contract surfaces — 28 customer endpoints + 6 cross-cutting; admin is backend-only per BA out_of_scope; sole owner of cookie↔Bearer translation per cross-cutting.auth.token_acquisition_flow, owns Idempotency-Key generation, integration surface for the entire customer journey)
complexity_rationale_legend.standard: identity (CRUD + JWT issuance + refresh rotation; tricky but bounded), catalog (CRUD + filtered listing + soft-delete event emission), cart (CRUD with status flagging)
complexity_rationale_legend.simple: (none — every component in this MVP carries either auth, state, or orchestration weight; tagging anything 'simple' would mislead Tech-Designer's model tier)

notes.required_rationale: All 8 are required:true. The BA success_conditions enumerate an end-to-end browse→cart→checkout→pay→track flow that involves every backend service and the frontend; if any component fails, the run can't ship the MVP.
notes.parallel_safe_rationale: All true. Tech-Designer fan-out reads the published contracts independently; no TD waits on another TD's output. Dev fan-out is similarly independent (different service repos, schema-per-service, contract-driven mocks).

components.complexity_rationale: Concurrent stock reservation under FOR UPDATE row lock with the no-negative invariant (CHECK constraint AND optimistic version), dual sync HTTP + async event-driven paths (events.payment.completed/failed/expired/order.cancelled all consumed state-driven per PR-003 race resolution), in-process sweeper (cross-cutting.pricing.constants.RESERVATION_TTL_MINUTES=15) using FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, outbox publisher for events.reservation.expired, and a documented lock-order rule for bulk reservation paths. Tech-Designer needs the higher model tier to author the lock-order pin + state-driven consumer logic without regressing the dry-run #1 PR-003 race.

10-step orchestration spanning 5 downstream services (cart, identity, catalog, inventory, order, payment) with a 4-branch compensation matrix; required Idempotency-Key per CHK-009 with the orderId-substitution rule at the internal boundary (cross-cutting.idempotency.internal_orderId_rule); server-side pricing tier under §11.2 with boundary-inclusive at 1500 THB; new buyerEmail dataflow via identity.profile.read step 2 (REV-L2-001 fix); requires saga reconciler for DEGRADED rows (REV-L2-008 followup). The compensation matrix alone forces TD into the higher model tier — it must author the failure_modes for steps 6/7/8 with idempotent rollback and audit logging without producing the dry-run #1 dead-end.

Sole writer of order.status (verified in dry-run #1 grep across 7 backends — only Order's storage_order.UpdateStatus mutates the column) AND the state machine owner for §9.2 transitions AND the consumer of 4 cross-topic events (events.payment.completed/failed/expired, events.order.cancelled fan-back into Inventory, events.reservation.expired) AND the producer of order.cancelled via outbox AND the recipient of the new internal create-from-checkout + cancel-on-checkout-failure routes. State-driven consumer rule (read current state via FOR UPDATE, ignore event.fromStatus) is load-bearing for the PR-003 race; mis-implementing it permanently corrupts orders. TD needs the higher tier to author all four event handlers + the two new internal handlers + the transitions table.

Idempotent webhook with strict (paymentIntentId, providerStatus) dedup keyed on a unique-constraint violation (replay returns cached envelope, never re-emits domain events); intent-create idempotent on orderId per the new internal_orderId_rule (REV-L2-006); outbox publisher for payment.completed/failed/expired with per-orderId partition; PAY-005/PAY-006/PAY-007 all interact with the dedup table; payment.intent.expiry-sweeper (60s) handles the no-callback-arrived case. Constant-time compare on X-Internal-Secret is mandatory (REV-L2-003). TD needs the higher tier to ship the dedup table + outbox + sweeper + constant-time middleware as one coherent story.

PR-007 + REV-L2-013 verification: 28 customer contract surfaces + 6 cross-cutting contracts (customer endpoints only; admin is backend-only via curl/Postman per BA out_of_scope and EPIC_FRONTEND); sole owner of the cookie↔Bearer translation pinned in cross-cutting.auth.token_acquisition_flow (read access cookie → forward Bearer; on miss/expiry call identity.refresh and rotate cookies; never expose JWT to JS); owns Idempotency-Key generation/persistence on the client (localStorage keyed per pending checkout); MUST NOT forward X-Internal-Secret and MUST NOT load INTERNAL_SHARED_SECRET (REV-L2-013 verified-correct posture). Sole integration surface for the entire customer journey — a defect in route-handler auth, idempotency wiring, or accidental internal-secret leakage blocks every functional Customer AC. Same yardstick as checkout (multi-step orchestration = complex).
